A.why: Only candidate with a true floor-length bell from the hip; reads as a gown from the ARPG camera and is distinct from all reference families.
A.fix: Halve the shoulder-width sleeves; add a white/tan hem or panel to lift the all-blue skirt and give the helm a swept wind crest.

B.why: Lovely cloud-white and steel palette with helm wings, but bright block sleeves dominate and the skirt only flares at a shin-length hem.
B.fix: Slim and darken the sleeves; start the flare at the hip and run it to the ankle; carry white onto the back of the skirt.

F.why: The best wind invention (swept ear crest, streamer), but the skirt is straight split panels showing the legs and the sleeves are blocky.
F.fix: Close the panels into a hip-to-ankle bell; slim the sleeves; enlarge the streamer.

D.why: A wide flat waist plate and saturated blue shoulder caps read as a knight; the skirt is a straight column.
D.fix: Remove the waist plate and shoulder caps; flare the skirt from the hip; mute the royal blue.

E.why: Short tiered lamellar skirt with legs showing and a spike plume read as soldier armour, not a gown.
E.fix: Replace the tiers with a long flared skirt; slim the sleeves; swap the spike for a swept crest.

C.why: An oversized bodice slab wider than the shoulders, a straight column skirt and a bucket helm: bulky, not feminine.
C.fix: Rebuild the bodice to torso width with slim sleeves; add a hip bell; replace the bucket helm.

notes: No candidate fully solved slim sleeves: every one still has shoulder-width upper-arm blocks. A is the only true bell skirt. B has the best palette and F the only real wind motif; a merge of A's skirt, B's colours and F's streamer and crest would be the target.
